description: Source of truth for the strict-safe subset runner. Every status in the generated coverage matrix is derived from an actual execution of these fixtures; nothing here asserts coverage.

rules.proof_rule: A signed add/sub/mul is admitted only when every operand's static range makes overflow impossible; otherwise STRICT rejects with CPLUS-ARITH.
A division/modulo is admitted only when the divisor is provably nonzero; a provably zero divisor is rejected by STRICT with CPLUS-ARITH.
A compile-time constant index i into a fixed array of length N is admitted only if 0 <= i < N; otherwise STRICT rejects with CPLUS-BOUNDS/CPLUS-SAFE-BOUNDS.
For a tracked heap allocation of S bytes passed to a callee, every dereference p[i] must be provable within S/sizeof(*p); interprocedural extent propagation rejects the violation.
Constant-extent arrays and loop-tracked VLAs are admitted; a sizeof whose VLA operand has side effects is not a safe constant expression and is rejected.
rules.trusted_boundary: VLA extents are not part of the plain-C ABI contract; use a fixed extent or cplus-managed allocation with an explicit length field.

require: sizeof on a VLA evaluates the expression at run time

rules.proof_rule: When no static extent proof exists, the operation is not admitted by proof; the emitted C+ guard checks the index against the tracked allocation length at run time and aborts on violation.
rules.runtime_check: C+ runtime emits a bounds guard; violation aborts with "C+ error: index N is outside the bounds of 'p' (length L)".

rules.proof_rule: A dereference of a pointer known to be null on any reaching path is rejected; admitted programs must guard the pointer before dereference.
Definite-assignment CFG analysis requires every variable to be assigned on every path reaching a read; a join with an unassigned path is rejected.
A dereference through an lvalue whose type is incompatible with the stored object's effective type is rejected (strict aliasing); byte copies via memcpy are admitted.
A managed or borrowed pointer whose owner's scope ends at the return edge cannot escape that scope; returning the pointee by value is admitted.
Once a tracked owner is released, any subsequent liveness check or dereference of the same pointer is a use-after-free and is rejected.
Each tracked owner must be released exactly once on each path; a second release of the same owner is rejected with CPLUS-OWNER.
Raw realloc is rejected because failure loses the original block; the accepted form is the C+ managed reallocation helper with an explicit success check.
rules.trusted_boundary: cplus_realloc / cplus_realloc_registered are the trusted boundary for resize; the plain C realloc contract is not admitted in the strict subset.

require: raw realloc can lose the original block

rules.proof_rule: The format argument of printf/fprintf/snprintf must be a string literal; a non-literal format string is rejected with CPLUS-FFI.
rules.trusted_boundary: Untrusted text crosses the FFI boundary only as a %s argument to a literal format string.

require: format string is not a string literal

rules.proof_rule: A signal/callback handler body may only call async-signal-safe functions; a non-async-signal-safe call in such a handler is rejected with CPLUS-FFI.
rules.trusted_boundary: Handler state is confined to volatile sig_atomic_t; all other work is deferred out of the callback.

rules.proof_rule: Control flow (return/goto/break) must not leave a defer/resource cleanup block; such a jump is rejected so the cleanup always runs.

require: cannot jump out of a defer cleanup

rules.proof_rule: At a control-flow join (phi/conditional expression), the worst-case index over all arms must be within the callee's proven extent; a single out-of-range arm is rejected.

require: chosen by conditional expression is out of bounds

rules.proof_rule: A thread function may not write a shared global without synchronization; unsynchronized shared writes are rejected with CPLUS-FFI.
rules.trusted_boundary: Shared mutable state must be confined to one thread or passed through an explicit synchronization primitive.

rules.proof_rule: At a call boundary, an argument proven null cannot be passed to a callee that dereferences it; the call is rejected with CPLUS-LIFETIME.
A resource-typed field/container object is linear: it may be passed by address but not copied by value into a second owner; a value copy is rejected.
